period_comparison: Based return words have length multiples of p and gains in Q. Sending a return gain to its length mod p-prime defines a surjection Q onto the multiples of p mod p-prime: close walks of the same gain with a common return from that lifted endpoint. Lengths of base returns generate pZ. The kernel is H, the zero-length gain subgroup: a difference with length a multiple of p-prime can have that length cancelled by an integer combination of zero-gain return words, whose lengths generate p-prime Z. Hence p-prime=p*[Q:H]. Each cyclic trial measures p-prime directly in the reachable positive-edge SCC.
conventions: The finite regular base is strongly connected. Each edge is a distinguishable history choice. The ring starts at (0,R); vertex 2x means (x,R), 2x+1 means (x,L). The two directions at site zero are the common read, except the explicit incompatible parity control. A Boolean target mask stores residue z in bit z.
algebra: Root path attributes are (length, additive gain). An edge yields the difference between the chosen route to its endpoint and the route through the edge (through minus chosen). Adjoin (0,q). The gcd h of residual lengths is the base period. The gcd D of absolute two-row determinants is the lattice index in Z^2. The zero-length gain subgroup has index D/h. A Bezout combination with length h fixes its drift per h ticks.
multiplicity: Both endpoint coins must realize every one of the q labels at the same time. For positive rows the integer witness gives each count explicitly. Prefixing j independently chosen same-length zero-gain closed walks multiplies every witness count by at least the displayed loop multiplicity to the power j. These counts precede any interference, record or probability assignment.
